decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004

Following practical completion of works a final Energy Performance Certificate with accompanying Building Regulations compliance report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Where applicable, a Display Energy Certificate shall be submitted within 18 months following first occupation. Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The residential units hereby permitted shall not be occupied until the Building Regulations Optional requirement G2 for water consumption of no more than 105 litres or less per head per day (excluding allowance of up to five litres for external water consumption) has been complied with. The measures shall thereafter be permanently retained.Reason: To promote water conservation and efficiency measures in all new developments and where possible in the retrofitting of existing stock in accordance with Policy SI 5 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy CP21 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010).

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the future number of occupiers on site have been provided within the development, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities to be retained permanently thereafter.Reason: To safeguard the amenity of the occupiers of adjoining premises; protect the general environment; prevent any obstruction to pedestrian movement and to ensure that there are adequate facilities for the storage and recycling of recoverable materials.

No flat shall be occupied until space has been laid out within the site in accordance with drawing ref: Proposed Site Plan 62PL/04/2026 - PL20 for:o	The provision of 11 long stay and 2 short stay cycle parking spaces in an accessible location. The access route to the store should be a minimum of 1.2m wide to enable the bike to enter the store, should be step free and involve no more than 2 doors or gate (excluding the store door).o	Secured  with a British Standard mortice lock or access fob  The approved details shall thereafter be installed and permanently retained for cycle parkingo	Fully enclosed by 4 walls and a roofo	Ability to lock a bicycle to a permanent fixture (e.g. Sheffield stand or wall anchor)  The approved details shall thereafter be installed and permanently retained for cycle parkingReason: To encourage sustainable means of transport, to provide secure cycle storage facilities free from obstruction, and in the interest of visual amenity.

Prior to the commencement of above ground works of the development hereby permitted, details including photographs of samples to be used in the external elevations shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall thereafter be built in accordance with the approved details. The following details are required:a)	External facing materials including manufacturer specification of all facing materials and finishes including windows/doors, balustrades, privacy screens and rainwater goods;b)	Soft and hard landscaping including access paths and boundary treatment;c)	Details of the cycle store and refuse/recycling store, including materials, finishes and any green/sedum roof;d)	Details of any external lighting;e)	Details of the front lightwell screening and revised lightwell design, including scaled plans and sections demonstrating that the basement lightwell serving Bedroom 1 shall be at least 1.5 metres in depth.Reason: To ensure sustainable design and to ensure the external appearance of the building is satisfactory and that it protects the character and appearance of the surrounding area.

No development, including site preparation, demolition or construction works, shall commence until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Construction Management Plan shall include details of construction vehicle routing, access and egress arrangements, hours of deliveries, on-site storage of materials and plant, contractor parking, wheel washing facilities, measures to control dust, noise and vibration, and a photographic condition survey of the adjoining public highway, including the carriageway, footway, kerbs, crossover and any street furniture adjacent to the site, prior to commencement of works. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Construction Management Plan.Reason: To avoid obstruction and hazard to users of the public highway, to protect the condition of the highway, and to safeguard the amenities of neighbouring occupiers during construction.

Prior to the commencement of construction works, an updated flood risk assessment and a SuDS Strategy Report to provide further groundwater and surface water drainage details must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submitted details shall include:1. Further information to demonstrate that groundwater risk has been adequately assessed, including consideration of winter groundwater levels, given that the submitted geological investigation was undertaken in summer 2022;2. Details of any mitigation measures required around the proposed basement should groundwater levels rise, including any drainage and/or filter drains;3. Revised and dimensioned details of the proposed filter drain, including cross-sections, depth, construction details and explanation of the impermeable layer shown at the top of the filter trench;4. Confirmation of how the proposed filter drain would be hydraulically connected and how water would flow around the proposed basement without increasing flood risk to neighbouring properties;5. A technical note explaining the purpose, operation and direction of flow of the proposed filter drain and associated mitigation measures; and justification for why the proposed permeable paving is lined.The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure that the proposed basement extension and associated drainage measures would not increase groundwater or surface water flood risk to neighbouring properties, and to ensure that the proposed SuDS and mitigation measures are appropriate, in accordance with London Plan Policies SI12 and SI13, Core Strategy Policies 21 and 28, and DMD Policies 59, 60, 61 and 62.

Prior to the commencement of construction works, details of acoustic insulation between the approved flats, particularly where living areas are located above or below bedrooms, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved insulation shall be installed prior to occupation and retained thereafter.Reason: To ensure acceptable living conditions for future occupiers and to prevent unacceptable noise transfer between units.
